evidence_quotes: Tobelo, Indonesia led all regions with 12 events, followed closely by Nikolski, Alaska (11) and Mohr, Iran (10)
Daily counts surged to 9 events on both February 3 and February 14
shallow quakes (under 10 km) near Tual, Indonesia (2.0 km), Mohr, Iran (1.9 km), and Hachinohe, Japan (1.6 km)
⚠️ Mohr, Iran: Ten events in three weeks... conditions that amplify casualty risk if magnitudes escalate
This report is based on synthetic USGS-format data... should not be used for official emergency planning
criticisms: No concrete 24-hour actions are specified — the report never tells a coordinator to 'alert county X', 'request USGS update on Y', 'verify shelter capacity in Z', or take any other executable step.

Monitoring priorities are vague: 'warrants close monitoring' and 'close monitoring' are not specific watch items — no magnitude thresholds, no specific depth bands to watch, no trigger criteria for escalation.
The data caveat at the end ('should not be used for official emergency planning') actively undermines operational utility and contradicts the purpose of the report.
No next-7-days framing or time-bounded watch window is provided, making it impossible to set a review cadence or escalation timeline.
Prioritization is partially visible (three ⚠️ items) but all three are weighted equally with no explicit 'highest priority' designation or ranking rationale for resource pre-positioning decisions.

La Tirana, Chile (8 events, 4th most active) and Lata, Solomon Islands (7 events) are mentioned in the digest but absent from the Risk Watch section without explanation, leaving gaps in regional coverage.
